html:
The Mohawk, or Kanienʼkehá꞉ka ("people of the flint"), are an Iroquoian people of the Mohawk River valley in what is now New York. They were the easternmost nation of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy, keepers of its eastern door.

In the 1600s they traded with the Dutch at Fort Orange and got guns early. That helped them in the Beaver Wars, when they fought the Mohicans, the Wendat and the French of New France. Jesuit missions drew some Mohawk to settlements near Montreal, such as Kahnawake, where Kateri Tekakwitha lived. In the American Revolution most sided with Britain under Joseph Brant and afterwards moved to Canada, to the Grand River and Bay of Quinte.

Mohawk communities today straddle the border between the United States and Canada, at Akwesasne, Kahnawake, Kanesatake and elsewhere. Mohawk ironworkers became famous for building the skyscrapers and bridges of New York City.
